To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C30C32S substitution of the HIV Tat protein does not moderate neuropsychological functioning in clade C HIV infection.
the C31 substitution in Tat does not moderate cognitive outcomes in clade-C HIV-infected individuals.
The C31S dicysine motif substitution of Tat is not associated with better cognitive function in clades C-infected individuals.
